Reproducing Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene & Pakhomov (2025) from the DANDI datasets it names¶

Paper. Semenov I, Kim V, Silkuniene G, Pakhomov AG (2025). Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves for temporal interference stimulation. Cell Reports Physical Science 6, 102660. doi:10.1016/j.xcrp.2025.102660.

Text the claims file was written from. The NIH author manuscript (NIHMS2098259, PMC12320893) as served by Europe PMC, with its supplement (Figures S1 to S4, Table S1); the version of record was not read. The paper reports no original code.

Dataset. The target is DANDI:001048, version 0.250701.1624, its only published version, pinned for that reason. It names the paper as related, but it holds TIRF images of HEK cells under patch clamp from another study ("Plasma membrane conductance changes in response to supraphysiological hyperpolarization"), shown below. The paper's own data are in the ten dandisets its Data and code availability lists, and the claims file marks every claim data: elsewhere in them. Each is read at its only published version, the most recent:

Dandiset Version Holds Used for

001273 0.250805.1356 strobe imaging of 2-us pulses Figure 4
001274 0.250805.1401 strobe imaging of pulses and sine waves Figures 5, 6, S3

Every file is streamed from the archive; nothing is downloaded to disk. The paper does not say which figure is in which dandiset; the assignment is the claims file's, from the titles, and the data checks below are consistent with it.

Revision after the first verification round. The verifier was given the claims file of another dandiset (001274) for the same paper, so its claim ids and readings differ from this file's; its points on the code apply here as well and were taken up. The AP detector now asks for a width of 2 to 20 ms both at half the peak's dF and at half its prominence (section Readings; the first round used the prominence only, which counted small oscillations on a raised plateau as APs), and the single measures are shown as variants at the end. Added: a check that APs within 5 ms of onset are not onset artefacts, the late dF of the modulated and TTX sessions, the APs that remain in the 2-s sessions, the carrier phase of the strobe oscillations and the pulse onset. The strobe LOESS is now R's loess. Three claims whose size depends on calibrations or ROIs the dandisets do not hold are now blocked.

Revision after the second verification round. Text corrected where the outputs did not support it. Added: the session-description wording on TTX and vehicle (Data check), the O4 levels of the modulated session that decides fig2-modulated-locks-to-beats, and a box-size variant of the strobe ROIs (fig6-sine-less-than-pulse). fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher is now marked as resting on the crop ROI. For fig6-sine-less-than-pulse a change to blocked, metadata insufficient, is proposed for a third round, as for fig4-pooled-time-constants; its outcome is unchanged here.

Revision after the third verification round. The verifier agreed with the proposed change, and fig6-sine-less-than-pulse is now blocked, metadata insufficient. Added: the per-cycle reading with the full peak-to-peak amplitude, which the criterion names (the main table regresses half of it).

The notebook takes about 40 minutes, most of it streaming the strobe dandisets (about 11 GB of 001273 and the 001274 files of nine cells).

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import tisine as ts
pd.set_option("display.width", 200); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40); pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 200)
TL = ["001030", "001032", "001033", "001034", "001035", "001271", "001272"]

Load the data¶

Every time-lapse file is streamed and reduced, as it loads, to the soma dF traces under each ROI reading (O1 a, b and c) and F0 reading (O2 a and b). The strobe dandisets 001273 and 001274 are read later, file by file, in their own sections. Dandiset 001048, the one that names the paper, is listed and one of its files opened, to show what it holds.

# Contents of every dandiset the paper lists: titles, files, subjects, species, frame counts and rates.
for d in ["001030", "001031", "001032", "001033", "001034", "001035", "001271", "001272", "001273", "001274"]:
    m = ts.dandiset_meta(d)
    print(d, ts.VERSIONS[d], "|", m["name"][:100], "|", m["assetsSummary"]["numberOfFiles"], "files,",
          round(m["assetsSummary"]["numberOfBytes"] / 1e9, 2), "GB, species", [s["name"] for s in m["assetsSummary"].get("species", [])])
for d in TL:
    R = [r for r in REC[d] if "error" not in r]
    print(f"\n{d}: {len(R)} files, {len(set(r['subject_id'] for r in R))} subject ids, species {sorted(set(r['species'] for r in R))}")
    print("  subject descriptions:", sorted(set(r["subject_description"] for r in R)))
    print("  frames per file:", pd.Series([r['n_frames'] for r in R]).value_counts().to_dict(), "| rates (frames/s):", sorted(set(r['rate'] for r in R)))
    st = pd.DataFrame([r["stim"] for r in R])
    print("  stimuli:", st.groupby(["kind", "carrier", "mod"], dropna=False).size().to_dict())
    print("  TTX sessions:", int(st.ttx.sum()), "| labelled volts from", st.volts.min(), "to", st.volts.max())
    print("  solution NaCl:", sum("140 NaCl" in r["session_description"] for r in R), "NaGluconate:", sum("NaGluconate" in r["session_description"] for r in R))

# The clock: are APs locked to the stated stimulus onset? AP rate per 10-ms bin, before and after onset,
# over all 250-ms sessions with a stimulus (ROI c, F0 a, O3 a), and in sham sessions. APs are detected
# over the whole recording here (not only in the stimulus window) to show the contrast.
def all_peaks(d):
    out = []
    for r in REC[d]:
        if "error" in r or r["stim"]["kind"] not in ("sine", "mod", "sham"): continue
        dF, info = r["traces"][("c", "a")]
        pt, ph, pw = ts.detect_aps(r["t"], dF, 0, 1e9, info["pre_sd"], "a")
        out.append((r["stim"]["kind"], pt - r["onset"], r["t"][-1] - r["onset"], r["onset"]))
    return out
for d in ["001032", "001033", "001035", "001271", "001030"]:
    P = all_peaks(d)
    stim = [p for p in P if p[0] != "sham"]
    pre = sum(((x[1] > -x[3] + 3) & (x[1] < 0)).sum() for x in stim); pre_t = sum(x[3] - 3 for x in stim) / 1000
    dur = 2000 if d == "001030" else 250
    dur_n = sum(((x[1] >= 0) & (x[1] < dur)).sum() for x in stim); dur_t = sum(min(dur, x[2]) for x in stim) / 1000
    post = sum(((x[1] >= dur + 20)).sum() for x in stim); post_t = sum(max(0, x[2] - dur - 20) for x in stim) / 1000
    print(f"{d}: AP rate before onset {pre / pre_t:.2f}/s, during stimulus {dur_n / dur_t:.2f}/s, from 20 ms after its end {post / max(post_t, 1e-9):.2f}/s "
          f"(sessions {len(stim)}); sham sessions {sum(p[0] == 'sham' for p in P)}, APs in them {sum(len(p[1]) for p in P if p[0] == 'sham')}")
    if d == "001033":
        lat = np.concatenate([x[1] for x in stim]); h_, e_ = np.histogram(lat, bins=np.arange(-50, 341, 10))
        print("   001033 AP counts per 10 ms from -50 ms:", h_.tolist())

Checks of the metadata against the data:

  • 001048 holds TIRF images of HEK cells under patch clamp, with species human; it is another study. Its only link to this paper is the related-resource entry. The paper's data are in the ten dandisets its Data and code availability lists, and the claims file marks every claim data: elsewhere in them.
  • 001032 and 001034 hold the same 178 recordings, pixel for pixel, under different subject names (sub-N-1 in 001032 and sub-N-3 in 001034). They are counted once, from 001032.
  • The images are 16 x 16 pixels, where the paper describes 64 x 64 frames after binning; the depositors cropped each recording around the soma. Frame 0 of every file is a bright artefact and is dropped.
  • The frame rates are 3,086.4 frames/s (001032 to 001035, 001271, 001272) and 3,134.8 (001030), close to the paper's 3,086.4 and 3,130.
  • The APs start after the stated onset (50 ms; 25 ms in 001030) and the rate before it is low: this is consistent with the stated stimulus timing, which is not recorded in the files (no stimulus series). Sham sessions have no APs.
  • 001030 states mouse (Mus musculus, C57BL/6) neurons; the paper used only rat neurons. 001035 calls its neurons "C57BL/6 rat". 001030 makes each session a subject (sub-c7-1-45V); the neuron is read from the name.
  • The voltages are labelled "peak-to-peak" in 001032 to 001035 and "one polarity" in 001030, and the files say they are "not the actual amplitude measured on the oscilloscope", with frequency dependent calibration "reported separately". The calibration is not in the dandisets.
  • There are no NaGlu (low-conductivity) sessions with 250-ms waves anywhere: Figures 3A and 3B are not deposited. 001030 holds only the 2-s ramped waves of Figure 3C.
  • 001272 holds 3 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons; the paper reports 8.
  • 001032, 001033 and 001035 also hold sine waves of 20 Hz to 10 kHz, and 001033 and 001035 a few at 40 and 100 kHz, that the paper does not describe ("20Hz sine" in most neurons, frequency series in a few). They are not used.
  • The TTX session descriptions of 001271 (71 sessions) say TTX "abolished the action potentials and caused sustained depolarization", where the dandiset's description says TTX "completely prevented sustained depolarization". Every session description of 001272 says "without tetrodotoxin (vehicle control)", the wording of the 001271 vehicle sessions.

Readings and selections used by the claims¶

All claims on the time-lapse data are run under every combination of the readings the claims file names: ROI (O1) (a) the Otsu component nearest the centre, (b) that mask eroded by 2 pixels; F0 (O2) (a) all frames before onset, (b) the last 20 ms; AP height (O3) (a) above 5% dF, (b) above 5 SD of the pre-onset dF. A third ROI reading (c) is added: the whole 16 x 16 crop that the depositors cut around the soma. The paper measures "the emission intensity over the entire cell soma" (Methods, Recording of the optical APs); the crop is the dataset's own region of the soma, and the claims file says ROIs are taken from the dataset when it holds them (O1). The Otsu masks are small (a median of about 35 of 256 pixels, some of 1 to 3 pixels, above) and their pre-onset noise is about twice the crop's. The claims file's header blocks a claim whose readings disagree; protocol step 1.6 allows adopting the best-supported choice as an assumption instead. Where the ROI readings give different outcomes, the outcome is the one under the crop ROI, recorded as resting on that assumption (assumed), and every reading is shown.

AP detection (O3): a local maximum of dF above the height reading, at least 5 ms from a larger one, with a width at half height of 2 to 20 ms. The width is measured both at half the peak's dF (its height above F0) and at half its prominence (its rise above the neighbouring troughs), and must be 2 to 20 ms under both. Each measure alone fails here: at half the dF, small wiggles on the tail of an AP count as APs 5 ms later (maximum rates of 136 to 182 Hz and up to 18 APs in a modulated session); at half the prominence, small oscillations on a raised plateau count as APs, so that the claims file's sustained depolarization (no AP in the last 100 ms) can hardly occur. Requiring both is an assumption made here, in line with the paper's "brief emission upticks"; both single measures are run at the end (AP detector variants).

The 250-ms FluoVolt neurons are those of 001032, 001033 and 001035 (001034 is a copy of 001032). Stimuli are 2 and 20 kHz, unmodulated ("sine") or modulated at 20 Hz ("spindle" in the files). Traces are not corrected for bleaching: the claims file (F2) says the paper corrected only the 2-s recordings of Figure 3C.

ap-selection¶

Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization (mean of 22).

Per neuron, the mean peak dF and duration of its APs in the 250-ms FluoVolt sessions (every stimulus in 001032, 001033 and 001035), then the mean and SEM over neurons. Which APs: (a) every AP, (b) the first AP of each session. Duration: (a) width at half height, (b) from the rise to the first return to F0. Expected: 11.3 +- 0.9 % dF and 8 +- 0.7 ms.

In [10]:
rows = []
for r in RD:
    g = rd(FL_ALL[FL_ALL.kind.isin(["sine", "mod"])], r)
    g = g[g.n_ap > 0]
    for which in ["every", "first"]:
        for dur in ["half_width", "return"]:
            per = []
            for n, x in g.groupby("neuron"):
                if which == "every":
                    h = np.concatenate(x.ap_h.values); w = np.concatenate((x.ap_w if dur == "half_width" else x.ap_ret).values)
                else:
                    h = np.array([v[0] for v in x.ap_h]); w = np.array([v[0] for v in (x.ap_w if dur == "half_width" else x.ap_ret)])
                per.append((h.mean(), w.mean()))
            per = np.array(per)
            rows.append(dict(o1=r[0], o2=r[1], o3=r[2], aps=which, duration=dur, neurons=len(per),
                             peak=per[:, 0].mean(), peak_sem=stats.sem(per[:, 0]), dur_ms=per[:, 1].mean(), dur_sem=stats.sem(per[:, 1])))
APS = pd.DataFrame(rows)
APS["peak_ok"] = (APS.peak - 11.3).abs() <= 0.9
APS["dur_ok"] = (APS.dur_ms - 8).abs() <= 0.7
print(APS.round(2).to_string())
print("\nreadings with both within the SEM:", int((APS.peak_ok & APS.dur_ok).sum()), "of", len(APS))

Result: partially reproduced. Over 39 neurons the mean AP peak is within 11.3 +- 0.9 % dF in 12 of 16 readings under the crop ROI (c), 10.27 to 11.46 %, but the duration matches 8 +- 0.7 ms under no reading with that ROI: the width at half height is 3.11 to 3.71 ms and the rise-to-return duration 17.31 to 24.14 ms, the latter lengthened by the noise around F0. Under ROI (a) the peak is within the SEM in all 16 readings (11.01 to 11.56 %) and the duration in none (2.76 to 3.05 ms half width, 11.97 to 18.68 ms rise to return). Under ROI (b) the peak is 12.68 to 14.67 %, outside it, and three readings give a rise-to-return duration in range (7.32 to 8.57 ms). The peak holds under the crop ROI, taken as the paper's whole soma (an assumption); the duration holds under no reading in which the peak holds.

fig1-pure-sine-excites-all¶

Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested; near threshold isolated APs came 100 to 200 ms after onset, and stronger fields shortened the delay and evoked sustained firing whose maximum rate rose linearly to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz.

Per neuron and frequency (unmodulated sessions): excited when any session has an AP; the threshold is the lowest labelled voltage with an AP (F5) and the latency there the mean first-AP latency of the sessions at that voltage. Spearman rho of latency on voltage over a neuron's sessions with APs (at least 3 sessions at 2 or more voltages, a standard choice). The highest maximum firing rate of each neuron (inverse of its first inter-AP interval, F4) over both frequencies, readings (a) the median over neurons in 54 to 99 Hz, (b) at least 75% of neurons in 54 to 99 Hz.

In [12]:
def fig1(g):
    g = g[g.kind == "sine"]
    out = {}
    for f, x in g.groupby("carrier"):
        ex = x.groupby("neuron").n_ap.max() > 0
        out[f"excited_{int(f/1000)}k"] = ex.mean() * 100; out[f"n_{int(f/1000)}k"] = len(ex)
    lat, rho = [], []
    for (n, f), x in g.groupby(["neuron", "carrier"]):
        y = x[x.n_ap > 0]
        if len(y) == 0: continue
        v0 = y.volts.min(); lat.append(y[y.volts == v0].latency.mean())
        if len(y) >= 3 and y.volts.nunique() >= 2:
            rho.append(stats.spearmanr(y.volts, y.latency)[0])
    rho = np.array(rho); lat = np.array(lat)
    mr = g.groupby("neuron").max_rate.max().dropna()
    out.update(median_latency_at_threshold=np.median(lat), n_lat=len(lat), rho_neg=(rho < 0).sum(), n_rho=len(rho),
               rho_median=np.median(rho), max_rate_median=mr.median(), frac_rate_in_54_99=((mr >= 54) & (mr <= 99)).mean() * 100,
               n_rate=len(mr), max_rate_min=mr.min(), max_rate_max=mr.max())
    out["holds_a"] = (out["excited_2k"] >= 90 and out["excited_20k"] >= 90 and 90 <= out["median_latency_at_threshold"] <= 220
                      and out["rho_neg"] > out["n_rho"] / 2 and 54 <= out["max_rate_median"] <= 99)
    out["holds_b"] = (out["excited_2k"] >= 90 and out["excited_20k"] >= 90 and 90 <= out["median_latency_at_threshold"] <= 220
                      and out["rho_neg"] > out["n_rho"] / 2 and out["frac_rate_in_54_99"] >= 75)
    return out

    y = x.dropna(subset=["max_rate"])

Result: partially reproduced. Under the crop ROI unmodulated waves excited 27 of 28 neurons at 2 kHz (96.4 %) and 15 of 17 at 20 kHz (88.2 % with O3 a, 94.1 % with O3 b), and the first-AP latency fell with voltage in 34 of 37 neuron-frequencies (35 of 38 with O3 b). The other two parts fail under every reading: the median latency at threshold is 59.8 to 88.4 ms (59 ms at 2 kHz and 124 ms at 20 kHz under ROI c), and the median highest maximum firing rate is 22.6 to 42.3 Hz, with 9.1 to 31.0 % of neurons in 54 to 99 Hz. Two of the 42 latencies at threshold (ROI c) are under 5 ms; without them the median is 63.9 ms instead of 60.8. APs this early are not onset artefacts: the same stimulus under TTX gives no transient above 5 % in the first 10 ms in any of 71 sessions, against 145 of 211 without TTX. Under the Otsu ROIs fewer neurons reach the AP height (39.3 to 85.7 % excited at 2 kHz). Below each neuron's highest rate the rate rises with voltage (slope positive in 23 of 23 neurons, not deciding).

fig1-excitation-block¶

At the highest fields, unmodulated sine waves merged APs into low-amplitude oscillations on a continuous depolarization, which could flatten and leave the membrane depolarized for the rest of the stimulus (an excitation block), and this depolarization reversed immediately when the stimulus stopped.

Per neuron and frequency (unmodulated): the voltage giving the highest maximum firing rate; neurons tested above it; sustained depolarization (O4: no AP in the last 100 ms of the stimulus and mean dF there above (a) 5 SD of pre-onset dF or (b) half the neuron's median AP height) at their highest voltage; and the mean dF over the 50 ms after the stimulus, below the O4 level. Sessions of 900 frames end at 291 ms, before the stimulus ends, so their post-stimulus window is missing.

In [15]:
def block(g, o4):
    g = g[g.kind == "sine"]
    medh = g.groupby("neuron").ap_h.apply(lambda s: np.median(np.concatenate(s.values)) if len(np.concatenate(s.values)) else np.nan)
    res = []
    for (n, f), x in g.groupby(["neuron", "carrier"]):
        y = x.dropna(subset=["max_rate"])
        if len(y) == 0: continue
        vbest = y.loc[y.max_rate.idxmax(), "volts"]
        if x.volts.max() <= vbest: continue
        top = x[x.volts == x.volts.max()]
        s = [ts.sustained(row, medh[n], o4) for _, row in top.iterrows()]
        sus = any(v[0] for v in s)
        post = [row.mean_post50 < lvl for (_, row), (ok, lvl) in zip(top.iterrows(), s) if ok and np.isfinite(row.mean_post50)]
        res.append(dict(neuron=n, carrier=f, sustained=sus, post_below=all(post) if post else np.nan, n_post=len(post)))
    return pd.DataFrame(res)
rows = []
for r in RD:
    for o4 in "ab":
        b = block(rd(FL, r), o4)
        rows.append(dict(o1=r[0], o2=r[1], o3=r[2], o4=o4, tested_above=len(b), sustained=int(b.sustained.sum()),
                         post_checked=int(b.n_post.gt(0).sum()), post_below=int((b.post_below == True).sum()),
                         holds=b.sustained.sum() > len(b) / 2 and (b.post_below == True).sum() == b.n_post.gt(0).sum()))
BLK = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(BLK.to_string())

Result: not reproduced. Of the 12 to 14 neuron-frequencies tested above the voltage of their highest firing rate under the crop ROI, none shows sustained depolarization (O4, either level) at its highest voltage. Under ROI (a) 2 of 12 to 15 do, one of which falls below the O4 level within 50 ms of the stimulus end; under ROI (b) 1 of 4 to 13 under O4 (b) and none under O4 (a). Most neurons still fire in the last 100 ms at their highest voltage. Two sessions at any voltage meet O4 (a) under the crop ROI (001032/12_1 at 15 V, with no AP at all and a mean dF of 9.82 % in the last 100 ms, and 001033/3_2 at 9 V), and the mean dF in the last 100 ms rises with voltage (Spearman rho median 0.93, positive in 42 of 45 neuron-frequencies), so a depolarization builds up, but the block the claim describes is rare. 001032/12_1 stays depolarized after the stimulus (7.87 % over the next 50 ms), against the claim's immediate reversal. The traces are not corrected for bleaching (F2); the mean dF in the 50 ms after the stimulus is mostly below 0, so bleaching lowers the late dF by up to a few percent, which works against finding the block.

Thresholds (fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field, fig2d-5ap-above-1ap, fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher)¶

Per neuron and stimulus (2 or 20 kHz, modulated or not), the lowest labelled voltage with at least 1 and at least 5 APs in the 250-ms stimulus (F5). Neurons that never reached the count are left out of that mean (counted below). Ratios do not depend on the conversion of volts to V/cm, but they depend on the files' labelled voltages being in the same proportion to the true amplitude at 2 and 20 kHz, which the files say they are not ("calibration factors are frequency-dependent").

In [17]:
def thresholds(g):
    return g.groupby(["neuron", "stim"]).apply(lambda x: pd.Series(dict(t1=ts.threshold(x.volts, x.n_ap, 1), t5=ts.threshold(x.volts, x.n_ap, 5),
                                                                       vmax=x.volts.max())), include_groups=False).reset_index()
TH = {r: thresholds(rd(FL, r)) for r in RD}
th = TH[("c", "a", "a")]

                             n5=("t5", "count"), t5_mean=("t5", "mean"), t5_sem=("t5", "sem")).round(2).to_string())

fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field¶

All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.

Ratio of the mean 20-kHz to the mean 2-kHz threshold for each stimulus type and AP count (expected 2 +- 0.2), and two-tailed unpaired t tests: (a) one per type and count, each p < 0.0001, (b) one pooling the four.

In [18]:
rows = []
for r in RD:
    th = TH[r]
    d = dict(o1=r[0], o2=r[1], o3=r[2])
    a20, a2, ps = [], [], []
    for typ in ["pure", "mod"]:
        for k in ["t1", "t5"]:
            x20 = th[th.stim == f"{typ}_20k"][k].dropna(); x2 = th[th.stim == f"{typ}_2k"][k].dropna()
            d[f"ratio_{typ}_{k}"] = x20.mean() / x2.mean()
            p = stats.ttest_ind(x20, x2).pvalue if len(x20) > 1 and len(x2) > 1 else np.nan
            d[f"p_{typ}_{k}"] = p; d[f"n_{typ}_{k}"] = f"{len(x20)}/{len(x2)}"
            a20 += list(x20); a2 += list(x2); ps.append(p)
    d["p_pooled"] = stats.ttest_ind(a20, a2).pvalue
    ratios = [d[f"ratio_{t}_{k}"] for t in ["pure", "mod"] for k in ["t1", "t5"]]
    d["ratios_ok"] = all(abs(x - 2) <= 0.2 for x in ratios if np.isfinite(x)) and all(np.isfinite(ratios))
    d["holds_a"] = d["ratios_ok"] and all(np.isfinite(p) and p < 1e-4 for p in ps)
    d["holds_b"] = d["ratios_ok"] and d["p_pooled"] < 1e-4
    rows.append(d)
R20 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
with pd.option_context("display.float_format", "{:.3g}".format):
    print(R20.to_string())

11 neurons with both: ratio median 3.36, range 1.79 to 4.17; paired t p = 1e-06

Result: blocked, metadata insufficient. The claim is a ratio of fields in V/cm at 20 and 2 kHz. The files give labelled generator voltages and say the delivered amplitude differs from the label by frequency-dependent calibration factors "reported separately", which are in none of the dandisets, so the ratio cannot be formed. Shown, not deciding: in labelled volts the 20-kHz thresholds are higher in every reading (pooled p 2.5e-06 to 2.2e-24; under the crop ROI unmodulated p 5.1e-10 to 8.2e-10 for 1 AP and 1.9e-12 to 4.1e-12 for 5 APs), with ratios of the means of 2.33 to 2.80 under the crop ROI (2.04 to 3.52 over all readings), outside 2 +- 0.2; within the 11 neurons tested at both frequencies the median ratio is 3.36. The 20-kHz modulated group has 3 neurons. The first round recorded this claim as partially reproduced.

Result: reproduced, resting on the crop ROI. Under the crop ROI the mean 5-AP threshold is above the mean 1-AP threshold for all four stimuli in all four F0 and O3 readings (F0 a, O3 a: 5.00 against 4.22 V for pure 2 kHz, 6.15 against 5.38 for modulated 2 kHz, 13.55 against 9.85 for pure 20 kHz and 17.20 against 14.00 for modulated 20 kHz, where 2 of 3 neurons reach 5 APs). Under the Otsu ROIs at most 1 neuron reaches 5 APs with modulated waves, so those comparisons cannot be made, and under ROI (b) with O3 (a) the 5-AP mean is below the 1-AP mean for pure 2 kHz (4.65 against 4.85 V, over 4 and 22 neurons) and pure 20 kHz (12.00 against 12.33 V, over 1 and 9), means over different neurons. Within a neuron the 5-AP threshold cannot be below its 1-AP threshold.

fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher¶

Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier frequency for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds; the 2-kHz unmodulated AP threshold was 57.7 +- 3.6 V/cm.

Two-tailed unpaired t tests (Figure 2D legend), with a paired test over neurons tested with both as a variant. The 2-kHz unmodulated threshold in V/cm from the labelled peak-to-peak volts under the two field readings (36 V/cm per volt of amplitude, half the peak-to-peak value; or per volt peak to peak), for the 1-AP and the 5-AP threshold.

            m = th[th.stim == f"mod_{car}"][k].dropna(); p_ = th[th.stim == f"pure_{car}"][k].dropna()
            t = stats.ttest_ind(m, p_) if len(m) > 1 and len(p_) > 1 else None
            d[f"{car}_{k}"] = f"{m.mean():.2f} vs {p_.mean():.2f}, p={t.pvalue:.3g}" if t else f"n={len(m)}/{len(p_)}"
            d[f"up_{car}_{k}"] = bool(t is not None and m.mean() > p_.mean() and t.pvalue < 0.05)
            d[f"down_{car}_{k}"] = bool(t is not None and m.mean() < p_.mean() and t.pvalue < 0.05)
    x = th[th.stim == "pure_2k"]
    for fr, fac in ts.FIELD_READINGS.items():

    d["value_ok"] = any(abs(d[f"Vcm_{fr}_{k}"] - 57.7) <= 3.6 for fr in ts.FIELD_READINGS for k in ["t1", "t5"])
    d["tests_ok"] = d["up_2k_t5"] and d["up_20k_t1"] and d["up_20k_t5"] and not d["down_2k_t1"]
    rows.append(d)

Result: partially reproduced. Under the crop ROI modulated thresholds are higher than unmodulated ones in every comparison, but only one of the paper's three significant differences is significant here: 20 kHz with 1 AP, p = 0.034 under O3 (a) (0.10 under O3 b), with 3 modulated neurons. 20 kHz with 5 APs gives p = 0.13 (2 neurons) and 2 kHz with 5 APs p = 0.12 (paper 0.0079). 2 kHz with 1 AP does not differ the other way (p = 0.056, modulated higher). Paired within neurons, the 2-kHz 1-AP threshold is higher with modulation in 11 of 12 (p = 7.9e-05). Under the Otsu ROIs no test reaches p < 0.05. The mean unmodulated 2-kHz threshold is 4.22 V peak to peak, 76.0 V/cm (1 AP) or 90.1 V/cm (5 APs) if 36 V/cm applies to the amplitude and twice that if to the peak-to-peak value, none within 57.7 +- 3.6; the files say the delivered amplitude is "somewhat smaller" than the label and the calibration is not deposited, so this part cannot be judged. With the first round's detector (AP detector variants) the 20-kHz tests give p = 0.021 and 0.031 and the 2-kHz 5-AP test p = 0.09.

fig2-modulated-locks-to-beats¶

With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.

The files hold no stimulus waveform, so the envelope phase takes the claims file's two readings: (a) beat peaks 25 ms into each 50-ms beat, (b) at 0, 50, 100, 150 and 200 ms. Within 12.5 ms of a peak, pooled over sessions with at least 5 APs (and per session as a variant). The phase locking itself, whatever the phase, is shown by the vector strength of AP times at 20 Hz with a Rayleigh test.

In [23]:
def beats(g, o4, base=None):
    base = FL if base is None else base
    g = g[g.kind == "mod"].copy()
    medh = rd(base, (g.o1.iloc[0], g.o2.iloc[0], g.o3.iloc[0])).groupby("neuron").ap_h.apply(
        lambda s: np.median(np.concatenate(s.values)) if len(np.concatenate(s.values)) else np.nan)
    d = dict(sessions=len(g), max_aps=int(g.n_ap.max()), over10=int((g.n_ap > 10).sum()))
    sus = [ts.sustained(row, medh[row.neuron], o4)[0] for _, row in g.iterrows()]
    d["sustained"] = int(np.sum(sus))
    s5 = g[g.n_ap >= 5]
    ph = np.concatenate([(x - 50.0) % 50.0 for x in s5.ap_t]) if len(s5) else np.array([])
    d["sessions_5ap"] = len(s5); d["aps"] = len(ph)
    d["near_a"] = np.mean(np.abs(ph - 25) <= 12.5) if len(ph) else np.nan
    d["near_b"] = np.mean((ph <= 12.5) | (ph >= 37.5)) if len(ph) else np.nan
    per_a = [np.mean(np.abs(((x - 50) % 50) - 25) <= 12.5) > 0.5 for x in s5.ap_t]
    d["sessions_major_a"] = int(np.sum(per_a))
    ang = 2 * np.pi * ph / 50.0
    vs = np.abs(np.mean(np.exp(1j * ang))) if len(ph) else np.nan
    d["vector_strength"] = vs; d["rayleigh_p"] = np.exp(-len(ph) * vs ** 2) if len(ph) else np.nan
    d["mean_phase_ms"] = (np.angle(np.mean(np.exp(1j * ang))) % (2 * np.pi)) / (2 * np.pi) * 50 if len(ph) else np.nan
    d["holds_a"] = d["over10"] == 0 and d["near_a"] > 0.5 and d["sustained"] == 0
    d["holds_b"] = d["over10"] == 0 and d["near_b"] > 0.5 and d["sustained"] == 0
    return d
BT = pd.DataFrame([dict(o1=r[0], o2=r[1], o3=r[2], o4=o4, **beats(rd(FL, r), o4)) for r in RD for o4 in "ab"])

Result: reproduced, resting on the envelope phase and the O4 level. No modulated session has more than 10 APs (at most 8, of 84 sessions). In the 16 sessions with at least 5 APs (crop ROI), 96.4 % of APs fall within 12.5 ms of beat peaks 25 ms into each beat (envelope reading a) and 3.6 % near peaks at the start of each beat (reading b); the APs lock to 26.6 ms of the 50-ms beat (vector strength 0.735, Rayleigh p = 2.0e-20), and the phase histograms peak 15 to 35 ms into the beat at both carriers. Reading (a), the wave starting at minimal amplitude, is adopted: the paper's Methods say the modulated strobe waves start at minimal amplitude, and under reading (b) the APs would sit at the envelope's minima, where the field is near zero. No modulated session shows sustained depolarization under O4 (b); under O4 (a) one does under the crop ROI (001032/2_1 at 11 V, 5.96 % with no AP in its last 100 ms, a 900-frame session cut at 291 ms), none under the Otsu ROIs. It is also the only modulated session with a last-100-ms mean dF above 5 %. Under the Otsu ROIs at most 1 session reaches 5 APs, so the locking is shown under the crop ROI.

fig2c-pure-more-aps¶

In the same neuron, the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated sine waves, and at the same field strength pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones.

Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and labelled voltage (AP counts averaged over repeated sessions); 1-AP thresholds compared within neurons tested with both.

rows = []
for r in RD:
    g = rd(FL, r)
    c = g.groupby(["neuron", "carrier", "volts", "kind"]).n_ap.mean().unstack("kind").dropna()
    th = TH[r]; out = dict(o1=r[0], o2=r[1], o3=r[2], pairs=len(c), pure_more=int((c.sine > c["mod"]).sum()),
                           mod_more=int((c["mod"] > c.sine).sum()), equal=int((c["mod"] == c.sine).sum()),
                           paired_t_p=stats.ttest_rel(c.sine, c["mod"]).pvalue if len(c) > 1 else np.nan,
                           mean_diff=(c.sine - c["mod"]).mean())
    lo = hi = n = 0
    for car in ["2k", "20k"]:
        pv = th.pivot(index="neuron", columns="stim", values="t1")
        if f"mod_{car}" in pv and f"pure_{car}" in pv:
            pv = pv[[f"mod_{car}", f"pure_{car}"]].dropna(); n += len(pv)
            lo += int((pv[f"pure_{car}"] < pv[f"mod_{car}"]).sum()); hi += int((pv[f"pure_{car}"] > pv[f"mod_{car}"]).sum())
    out.update(neurons_both=n, pure_threshold_lower=lo, pure_threshold_higher=hi)
    out["holds"] = out["pure_more"] > out["mod_more"] and lo > hi
    rows.append(out)
PC = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: reproduced, resting on the crop ROI. Under the crop ROI unmodulated waves gave more APs than modulated ones at the same carrier and voltage in 44 of 52 pairs against 2 (mean difference 3.35 APs, paired p = 1.2e-08), and the unmodulated 1-AP threshold was lower in 14 of 15 neurons tested with both (higher in none). Both parts hold in 11 of the 12 readings. Under ROI (b) with F0 (b) and O3 (b) the counts still favour pure waves (9 pairs against 6), but of the 3 neurons with both thresholds the pure one is lower in none and higher in 1.

fig3c-sustained-firing-2s¶

In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped up over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration; the firing rate rose with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization, which developed before the end of the ramp.

001030: four neurons (c5 to c8) in NaGlu, 2-s waves starting at 25 ms with a 250-ms ramp (session descriptions). Bleaching is corrected "by subtracting a trace without APs" (Methods, Recording of the optical APs; F2). Only one session in 001030 has no AP (c7 at 1.0 V), so the corrections are: (i) c7's AP-free trace subtracted from every session (the only one there is), (ii) none, as a variant. Per neuron, the criterion's three parts: APs in the last 250 ms of the stimulus at some voltage; the AP count rising with voltage up to some voltage; and at the highest voltage no AP and mean dF above the O4 level from 275 ms (250 ms after onset) to the end. The figure shows one neuron, so the criterion is taken to hold when one neuron meets all three (a reading made here).

R30 = [r for r in REC["001030"] if "error" not in r]
ref = [r for r in R30 if ts.neuron_of_001030(r["path"]) == "c7" and abs(r["stim"]["volts"] - 1.0) < 1e-6][0]
def fig3c(o1, o2, o3, corr, width_ref="both"):
    rows = []
    for r in R30:
        dF, info = r["traces"][(o1, o2)]
        t = r["t"]
        if corr == "c7_free":
            if r is ref: continue
            rd_, _ = ref["traces"][(o1, o2)]; n = min(len(dF), len(rd_)); dF = dF[:n] - rd_[:n]; t = t[:n]
        pre_sd = float(dF[t < 25].std())
        pt, ph, pw = ts.detect_aps(t, dF, 25, 2025, pre_sd, o3, width_ref)
        late = (t >= 275) & (t < 2025)
        rows.append(dict(neuron=ts.neuron_of_001030(r["path"]), volts=r["stim"]["volts"], n_ap=len(pt), last250=int((pt >= 1775).sum()),
                         aps_after_275=int((pt >= 275).sum()), mean_after_275=float(dF[late].mean()), pre_sd=pre_sd,
                         median_h=np.median(ph) if len(ph) else np.nan, t_end=float(t[-1])))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["neuron", "volts"])
def judge(df, o4):
    out = {}
    for n, x in df.groupby("neuron"):
        x = x.sort_values("volts"); top = x.iloc[-1]
        medh = np.nanmedian(x.median_h)
        lvl = 5 * top.pre_sd if o4 == "a" else 0.5 * medh
        rises = len(x) > 1 and x.n_ap.iloc[: int(np.argmax(x.n_ap.values)) + 1].is_monotonic_increasing and x.n_ap.values.argmax() > 0
        out[n] = dict(late_aps=bool((x.last250 > 0).any()), rises=bool(rises), block=bool(top.aps_after_275 == 0 and top.mean_after_275 > lvl),
                      top_volts=top.volts, top_mean=round(top.mean_after_275, 2), level=round(lvl, 2))
        out[n]["all3"] = out[n]["late_aps"] and out[n]["rises"] and out[n]["block"]
    return out
rows = []
for o1 in "cab":
    for o2 in "ab":
        for o3 in "ab":
            for corr in ["c7_free", "none"]:
                df = fig3c(o1, o2, o3, corr)
                for o4 in "ab":
                    j = judge(df, o4)
                    rows.append(dict(o1=o1, o2=o2, o3=o3, corr=corr, o4=o4, **{f"{n}": ("".join("Y" if v[k] else "-" for k in ["late_aps", "rises", "block"]))
                                                                               for n, v in j.items()}, holds=any(v["all3"] for v in j.values())))
F3C = pd.DataFrame(rows)

from scipy import signal as _sg
for n_, v_ in [("c7", 2.3), ("c8", 2.0)]:
    r = [r for r in R30 if ts.neuron_of_001030(r["path"]) == n_ and abs(r["stim"]["volts"] - v_) < 1e-6][0]
    dF0, _ = r["traces"][("c", "a")]; rd_, _ = ref["traces"][("c", "a")]; m = min(len(dF0), len(rd_)); dF = (dF0[:m] - rd_[:m]).astype(float); t = r["t"][:m]
    pre_sd = float(dF[t < 25].std())
    for wr in ["both", "prominence"]:
        pt, ph, pw = ts.detect_aps(t, dF, 25, 2025, pre_sd, "a", wr)
        sel = pt >= 275
        idx = np.searchsorted(t, pt[sel]); prom = _sg.peak_prominences(dF, idx)[0] if len(idx) else []
        print(f"{n_} {v_} V, width {wr}: {int(sel.sum())} APs after 275 ms at", np.round(pt[sel], 0).tolist(), "height", np.round(ph[sel], 1).tolist(),
              "prominence", np.round(prom, 1).tolist(), "width", np.round(pw[sel], 1).tolist())
    k = int(round(5.0 / np.median(np.diff(t))))
    pk, _ = _sg.find_peaks(dF, height=5.0, distance=k)
    rise = [p for p in pk if t[p] >= 275 and t[p] < 2025 and dF[p] - dF[max(0, p - k):p].min() >= 5.0]
    print(f"   rise of 5 % within 5 ms: {len(rise)} peaks after 275 ms; mean dF after 275 ms {dF[(t >= 275) & (t < 2025)].mean():.2f} %")

Result: partially reproduced. In all four neurons of 001030, under the crop ROI with the bleaching correction, some voltage gives APs in the last 250 ms of the 2-s wave (firing for the whole duration) and the AP count rises with voltage up to a point. No neuron, under any reading or correction, shows the third part, a block at the highest voltage, though c7 at 2.3 V comes close: 7 APs during the ramp and one after 275 ms (at 1,964 ms, 8.0 % high, prominence 4.4 %), on a mean dF of 6.72 %. The first round's detector counted 11 APs there, with prominences of 2.7 to 6.4 %. c8 at 2.0 V keeps 6 APs after 275 ms (prominence 4.1 to 7.2 %) on a mean dF of 3.63 %. At the top voltage the count falls (c7 from 88 to 8, c8 from 46 to 8) while the mean dF stays raised. Two c5 sessions end at 1,914 ms, before the stimulus ends.

figs1-di8-same-as-fluovolt¶

With Di-8-ANEPPS in place of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, 2-kHz sine waves near threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs, and stronger fields shortened the delay and induced sustained firing ending in sustained depolarization, as with FluoVolt.

001272, traces inverted (Di-8-ANEPPS emission falls with depolarization; F1). O3 reading (a) is used only if the inverted APs reach 5% (claims file); their heights are shown first. Per neuron: one to three APs at the lowest voltage with APs; Spearman rho of first-AP latency on voltage below 0; sustained firing (an AP in the last 100 ms of the stimulus, a standard choice) or sustained depolarization (O4) at a voltage above the lowest with APs.

Result: partially reproduced. 001272 holds 3 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, not the paper's 8. The inverted APs are small (median 4.2 % dF, 13 % of them above 5 %), so O3 reading (b) alone applies, as the claims file says. Under the crop ROI with O3 (b), most of the 3 neurons show one to three APs at their lowest voltage with APs (3 with F0 a, 2 with F0 b), a latency that falls with voltage (2 of 3, rho -0.03 and -0.69; -0.12 and -0.76 with F0 b) and sustained firing or depolarization at higher voltages (3 of 3). Under the Otsu ROIs with O3 (b) the latency falls in at most 1 of 3 and one or two neurons have no AP. The behaviour holds in the deposited neurons under the crop ROI (an assumption); the count of eight does not, five neurons not being deposited.

figs2-ttx-blocks-depolarization¶

1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization evoked by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves, while the vehicle did not.

  1. In TTX neurons the sessions before are those labelled vehicle and the sessions after those labelled TTX. Vehicle neurons have no label for the change of solution; their sessions fall into blocks separated by pauses of about 300 s, and the split is taken at the longest pause (an assumption; the pause is printed). Responses are compared at the voltages tested both before and after. A response is an AP in the stimulus or sustained depolarization (O4).
In [30]:
TT = TAB["001271"]
def ttx(r, o4, table=None):
    g = rd(TT if table is None else table, r); g = g[g.kind == "sine"]
    medh = g.groupby("neuron").ap_h.apply(lambda s: np.median(np.concatenate(s.values)) if len(np.concatenate(s.values)) else np.nan)
    rows = []
    for n, x in g.groupby("neuron"):
        b, a, gap = ts.split_before_after(x)
        common = sorted(set(b.volts) & set(a.volts))
        if not common:
            rows.append(dict(neuron=n, group="TTX" if x.ttx.any() else "vehicle", gap_s=gap, common_volts=0)); continue
        def resp(y):
            return [bool(row.n_ap > 0 or ts.sustained(row, medh[n], o4)[0]) for _, row in y[y.volts.isin(common)].iterrows()]
        def susd(y):
            return int(sum(ts.sustained(row, medh[n], o4)[0] for _, row in y[y.volts.isin(common)].iterrows()))
        rb, ra = resp(b), resp(a)
        rows.append(dict(neuron=n, group="TTX" if x.ttx.any() else "vehicle", gap_s=gap, common_volts=len(common),
                         before_resp=f"{sum(rb)}/{len(rb)}", after_resp=f"{sum(ra)}/{len(ra)}",
                         aps_before=int(b[b.volts.isin(common)].n_ap.sum()), aps_after=int(a[a.volts.isin(common)].n_ap.sum()),
                         sus_before=susd(b), sus_after=susd(a),
                         ok=(all(rb) and not any(ra)) if x.ttx.any() else all(ra),
                         ok_any=(any(rb) and not any(ra)) if x.ttx.any() else any(ra)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: partially reproduced. Under the crop ROI all 6 TTX neurons had APs before TTX at the voltages tested in both conditions and none responded after it (no AP and no sustained depolarization); after TTX the mean dF in the last 100 ms is at most 0.42 %. In 5 of the 6 (3 or 4 with F0 b) every session before TTX responded; in 001271/14_20240731 one of 8 did not. Sustained depolarization (O4) before TTX occurred only in that neuron (2 sessions; its median last-100-ms dF was 5.08 and 5.18 % at 4.5 and 5 V before TTX, and -0.46 and -0.66 % after), so the abolition of the depolarization rests on one neuron. 11 of 13 vehicle neurons responded at every common voltage after the pause, and all 13 at some. The two that did not at every voltage are 001271/4_20240730 (2 of 3), whose longest pause is 73 s, so no change of solution can be placed, and 001271/5_20240801 (5 of 7). The vehicle split is the longest pause, about 300 s in most neurons but 167 s in 001271/13_20240731 and 73 s in 001271/4_20240730 (35 s in 001271/17_20240801, which has no voltage in common). Under the Otsu ROIs at most 1 of the 6 TTX neurons responds at every voltage before TTX.

fig3-not-heating¶

Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, where it evoked sustained firing, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.

The rise is conductivity times E squared times duration over the volumetric heat capacity (water, 4.18 J per cm3 per K, the claims file's standard choice), with E the peak or the RMS field. These are calculations from the paper's own numbers; the Figure 3A neuron is not in the dandisets (no NaGlu 250-ms sessions).

In [32]:
def rise(E_vcm, sigma_mScm, t=0.25, rc=4.18e6):
    return sigma_mScm / 10 * (E_vcm * 100) ** 2 * t / rc
for name, E, s, exp in [("63 V/cm NaCl", 63, 16.4, 2.5), ("63 V/cm NaGlu", 63, 8.4, 1.24), ("81 V/cm NaCl", 81, 16.4, 4.1)]:
    print(f"{name}: peak {rise(E, s):.2f} C, RMS {rise(E, s) / 2:.2f} C, paper {exp}")
print("ratio 81/63 in NaCl: computed %.3f, paper %.3f (%.1f %% apart)" % ((81 / 63) ** 2, 4.1 / 2.5, 100 * abs((81 / 63) ** 2 / (4.1 / 2.5) - 1)))
print("ratio NaGlu/NaCl at 63: computed %.3f, paper %.3f (%.1f %% apart)" % (8.4 / 16.4, 1.24 / 2.5, 100 * abs((8.4 / 16.4) / (1.24 / 2.5) - 1)))
print("heat capacity that gives 2.5 C at 63 V/cm, peak field: %.2f J/cm3/K; RMS: %.2f" % (rise(63, 16.4) * 4.18 / 2.5, rise(63, 16.4) / 2 * 4.18 / 2.5))

63 V/cm NaCl: peak 3.89 C, RMS 1.95 C, paper 2.5
63 V/cm NaGlu: peak 1.99 C, RMS 1.00 C, paper 1.24
81 V/cm NaCl: peak 6.44 C, RMS 3.22 C, paper 4.1
ratio 81/63 in NaCl: computed 1.653, paper 1.640 (0.8 % apart)
ratio NaGlu/NaCl at 63: computed 0.512, paper 0.496 (3.3 % apart)
heat capacity that gives 2.5 C at 63 V/cm, peak field: 6.51 J/cm3/K; RMS: 3.25

Result: blocked, methods underspecified. With water's heat capacity, the peak field gives 3.89 C and the RMS field 1.95 C at 63 V/cm in NaCl, neither 2.5 C. The paper's three values scale as the formula says (81/63 squared is 1.653 against the paper's 1.640, 0.8 % apart; 8.4/16.4 is 0.512 against 0.496, 3.3 % apart), so its numbers are consistent with each other but come from a heat capacity or field the paper does not give (2.5 C needs 6.51 J per cm3 per K with the peak field). The Figure 3A neuron is not in the dandisets.

Strobe imaging: files and experiments¶

001273 (2-us pulses from two orthogonal directions, Figure 4) and 001274 (pulses and single beats of modulated 2-kHz sine waves, Figures 5, 6 and S3) hold full 512 x 512 frames and no ROIs. Their metadata are read first; the frames are streamed file by file in each section and reduced to ROI traces as they load.

In [33]:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import re
SM = {d: [r for r in ts.load_dandiset(d, with_data=False)] for d in ["001273", "001274"]}  # metadata only
def strobe_info(r):
    s = r["session_description"]
    v = re.search(r"at ([\d,.]+)\s*V amplitude", s)
    fm = re.search(r"modulated at ([\d.]+)\s*Hz", s)
    pos = "up/bottom" if "above (Up)" in s else ("right/left" if "Right and Left" in s else "not specified")
    kind = "pulse" if "rectangular pulse" in s else ("mod" if fm else "sine")
    return dict(path=r["path"], subject=r["subject_id"], start=r["start"], n=r["shape"][0], kind=kind, fm=float(fm[1]) if fm else np.nan,
                volts=float(v[1].replace(",", ".")) if v else np.nan, backward="backward manner" in s, position=pos,
                ttx="presence of the sodium channel inhibitor" in s, asset_id=r["asset_id"], dandiset=r["dandiset"])
url_cache = {}
def url_of(d, aid):
    if aid not in url_cache: url_cache[aid] = ts.s3_url(d, aid)
    return url_cache[aid]
def read_prepped(row):
    for k in range(4):
        try:
            x = ts.read_strobe(url_of(row.dandiset, row.asset_id)).astype(np.float32)
            break
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(3 + 3 * k)
    if row.backward: x = x[::-1]
    med, good = ts.frame_scale(x)
    return x, med, good

The paper's 19 Figure 4 experiments are cells in one field direction. 001273 has 22 groups of 7 or 8 replicates: on 2024-01-17 four cells at 40 V and again at 80 V with "electrode position not specified", on 2024-01-19 four cells with the electrodes up/bottom and right/left at 40 V and a fifth at 100 and 130 V, and on 2024-03-11 four cells up/bottom (one at 60 V). The paper gives 140 V/cm for all; which 19 groups are the paper's, and which cells are elongated or random, the files do not say. Two selections are run: (i) all 22 groups, (ii) the 15 groups at 40 V. In 001274 nine cells have a pulse and 2-kHz waves modulated at 100 Hz without TTX (2024-05-22 cells 2 to 4 and 2024-05-23 cells 2 to 7): these are taken as the nine cells of Figure 6. The paper does not mention TTX for these experiments, but 2024-08-24 sessions are labelled with TTX. The paper averaged 12 sine sessions for the Figure 5 cell; no cell in 001274 has more than 5 sessions at 100 Hz (2_20240522 has 5), so the Figure 5 and S3 cells (C7 and C8) cannot be identified.

fig4-pooled-time-constants¶

Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so the membrane charges fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.

Per experiment, the replicates are reversed where recorded backward, scaled (reading a) or not (b), and averaged; ROIs from the averaged scaled stack. The cathodic pole is the depolarized ROI, the anodic the hyperpolarized one. Charging fit over the pulse (frames 20 to 60), discharging fit from the pulse end to the last frame with (a) a free amplitude, (b) the amplitude fixed to the charging fit's value at the pulse end. Expected: 0.7 +- 0.08, 0.91 +- 0.08, 0.65 +- 0.05, 0.8 +- 0.07 us.

groups = [(k, g) for k, g in groups if len(g) >= 7]

rows = []; t0 = time.time()
for (subj, pos, volts), g in groups:
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
        reps = list(ex.map(read_prepped, [r for r in g.itertuples()]))
    acc = {"a": np.zeros((160, 512, 512), np.float32), "b": np.zeros((160, 512, 512), np.float32)}; cnt = np.zeros(160)
    for x, med, good in reps:
        acc["a"][good] += x[good] / med[good][:, None, None]; acc["b"][good] += x[good]; cnt += good
    goodall = cnt > 0
    for k in acc: acc[k][goodall] /= cnt[goodall][:, None, None]
    c1, c2, ratio, cell = ts.find_rois(acc["a"], goodall)
    for o5 in "ab":
        for pole, c in [("anodic", c1), ("cathodic", c2)]:
            dF = ts.pulse_dF(ts.box(acc[o5], c), goodall, slice(1, ts.PULSE_ON))
            A, tau_c = ts.fit_charging(tt[20:61], dF[20:61])
            for rdg in "ab":
                Afix = None if rdg == "a" else A * (1 - np.exp(-2.0 / tau_c))
                A2, tau_d = ts.fit_discharging(tt[60:] - 2.0, dF[60:], Afix)
                rows.append(dict(subject=subj, position=pos, volts=volts, replicates=len(g), o5=o5, pole=pole, fit=rdg,
                                 dFmax=A, tau_charge=tau_c, tau_discharge=tau_d, ratio_at_roi=ratio[c]))
    del acc, reps
print("read and fitted in %.0f s" % (time.time() - t0))
K4 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(K4[(K4.o5 == "a") & (K4.fit == "a")].round(2).to_string())

def pooled(df):
    out = {}
    for pole in ["cathodic", "anodic"]:
        x = df[df.pole == pole]
        out[f"{pole}_charge"] = f"{x.tau_charge.mean():.2f} +- {x.tau_charge.sem():.2f}"
        out[f"{pole}_discharge"] = f"{x.tau_discharge.mean():.2f} +- {x.tau_discharge.sem():.2f}"
        out[f"{pole}_charge_median"] = x.tau_charge.median(); out[f"{pole}_discharge_median"] = x.tau_discharge.median()
    exp = {"cathodic_charge": (0.7, 0.08), "cathodic_discharge": (0.91, 0.08), "anodic_charge": (0.65, 0.05), "anodic_discharge": (0.8, 0.07)}
    out["within_sem"] = sum(abs(float(out[k].split()[0]) - v) <= tol for k, (v, tol) in exp.items())
    return out

Result: blocked, metadata insufficient. The claim is a mean over the paper's 19 experiments, measured in hand-drawn ROIs. 001273 holds no ROIs and does not say which of its 22 groups are the 19 experiments; its groups were run at 40 to 130 V, whose session descriptions give measured amplitudes of 25 to 102 V, where the paper gives 140 V/cm for all. Shown, not deciding: with 12 x 12 pixel boxes at the extremes of the smoothed ratio image, no pooled mean is within the paper's SEM under any selection, scaling or discharging fit (0 of 4 in every row), 16 of 176 charging fits end at the 20-us bound, and the medians are 0.37 to 0.49 us (cathodic) and 0.57 to 1.02 us (anodic) for charging and 0.81 to 1.79 us for discharging, against 0.65 to 0.91 in the paper. The first round recorded this claim as not reproduced; the time constants depend on the ROIs and the selection, which the dandiset does not give.

fig6-sine-less-than-pulse¶

Across 9 cells FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-us pulses was 15% to 47% per 1 kV/cm (mean 28%); sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves, linearly correlated with the field, was 1.5% to 28.4% (mean 11.8%), smaller in every ROI, and 42% of the pulse value.

Per cell: ROIs from the pulse (above); pulse sensitivity, the mean dF over the 21 frames from 1 to 2 us into the pulse over 0.257 kV/cm, sign removed. Sine: the 2-kHz waves modulated at 100 Hz (four sessions per cell, five in 2_20240522), dF per session (F0 from the first and last cycles), averaged over sessions, the LOESS fit subtracted (R's loess, degree 2, as in RStudio, Table S1; O6: span 2 or 4 ms), and the oscillation regressed (a) on the signed field (sign removed after), (b) per carrier cycle, half the peak-to-peak amplitude on the cycle's peak field (half, so that it is on the scale of (a); the criterion names the full peak-to-peak amplitude, shown as a variant). Scaling O5 (a) or (b). As a check of the assumed carrier phase, the phase of the carrier in each ROI's oscillation is also fitted, with the sensitivity at that phase (variant c).

cells6 = []
for subj, g in S4[~S4.ttx].groupby("subject"):
    if (g.kind == "pulse").any() and ((g.kind == "mod") & (g.fm == 100)).any():
        cells6.append(subj)
print(len(cells6), "cells:", cells6)
def read_rois(row, centres):
    for k in range(4):
        try:
            x = ts.read_strobe(url_of(row.dandiset, row.asset_id)); break
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(3 + 3 * k)
    if row.backward: x = x[::-1]
    med, good = ts.frame_scale(x)
    tr = np.array([[ts.box(x, c, h) for c in centres] for h in ROI_HALVES])
    return tr, med, good
ROI_HALVES = [6, 3, 10]  # 12 x 12 boxes used; 6 x 6 and 20 x 20 as a variant (round-2 verifier: the sizes depend on the ROIs)
SENS = []; WHOLE = []; PULSE_TR = []; BOXV = []; t0 = time.time()
for subj in cells6:
    g = S4[(S4.subject == subj) & ~S4.ttx]
    pr = g[g.kind == "pulse"].sort_values("start").iloc[0]
    x, med, good = read_prepped(pr)
    xs = x / med[:, None, None]
    c1, c2, ratio, cell = ts.find_rois(xs, good)
    sess = list(g[(g.kind == "mod") & (g.fm == 100)].itertuples())
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
        sine = list(ex.map(lambda r: read_rois(r, (c1, c2)), sess))
    n = min(s[0].shape[-1] for s in sine)
    v_sine = g[(g.kind == "mod") & (g.fm == 100)].volts.iloc[0]
    epk = 0.136 * v_sine / 7.0  # 136 V/cm at the 7 V of the Figure 5 cell; scaled for cells run at another voltage
    epulse = 0.257 * pr.volts / 10.0  # 257 V/cm at 10 V, likewise
    t, E, env = ts.sine_field(n, 100.0, epk=epk)
    base = np.r_[0:25, n - 25:n]
    for o5 in "ab":
        P = xs if o5 == "a" else x
        for k, (roi, c) in enumerate([("ROI1", c1), ("ROI2", c2)]):
            dFp = ts.pulse_dF(ts.box(P, c), good, slice(1, ts.PULSE_ON))
            ps = np.nanmean(dFp[40:61]) / epulse
            run5 = pd.Series(dFp[ts.PULSE_ON:ts.PULSE_OFF + 1]).rolling(5, center=True).mean()
            peak5 = run5.abs().max() / epulse
            dfs = []
            for tr, m, gd in sine:
                F = tr[0, k, :n] / (m[:n] if o5 == "a" else 1.0); F = F.astype(float); F[~gd[:n]] = np.nan
                dfs.append(100 * (F / np.nanmean(F[base]) - 1))
            dF = np.nanmean(dfs, 0); ok = np.isfinite(dF)
            for span in [2.0, 4.0]:
                lo = ts.loess(t[ok], dF[ok], span / (n * 0.02))
                osc = dF[ok] - lo
                lr = stats.linregress(E[ok], osc)
                cyc = (t[ok] // 5e-4).astype(int)
                cp = pd.DataFrame(dict(c=cyc, o=osc, e=env[ok] * epk)).groupby("c").agg(p2p=("o", lambda v: v.max() - v.min()), epk=("e", "max"))
                lr_b = stats.linregress(cp.epk, cp.p2p / 2)
                phase, amp = ts.carrier_phase(t[ok], osc, env[ok])
                SENS.append(dict(cell=subj, roi=roi, o5=o5, span=span, pulse=abs(ps), pulse_peak5=peak5, pulse_signed=ps,
                                 sine_a=abs(lr.slope), sine_a_signed=lr.slope, p_a=lr.pvalue, sine_b=abs(lr_b.slope), p_b=lr_b.pvalue,
                                 sessions=len(sine), sine_volts=v_sine, pulse_volts=pr.volts, phase=phase, sine_c=amp / epk, pulse_frames=pr.n))
                if o5 == "a" and span == 2.0:
                    PULSE_TR.append(dFp * np.sign(ps))
                if o5 == "a":
                    WHOLE.append(dict(cell=subj, roi=roi, span=span, loess_at_peak=lo[np.argmax(env[ok])], osc=osc))
    # Box-size variant: scaled (O5 a), span 2 ms, signed regression, same centres.
    for hi, h in enumerate(ROI_HALVES[1:], 1):
        for k, c in enumerate((c1, c2)):
            dFp = ts.pulse_dF(ts.box(xs, c, h), good, slice(1, ts.PULSE_ON))
            ps = np.nanmean(dFp[40:61]) / epulse
            dfs = []
            for tr, m, gd in sine:
                F = (tr[hi, k, :n] / m[:n]).astype(float); F[~gd[:n]] = np.nan
                dfs.append(100 * (F / np.nanmean(F[base]) - 1))
            dF = np.nanmean(dfs, 0); ok = np.isfinite(dF)
            osc = dF[ok] - ts.loess(t[ok], dF[ok], 2.0 / (n * 0.02))
            lr = stats.linregress(E[ok], osc)
            BOXV.append(dict(cell=subj, roi=f"ROI{k + 1}", half=h, pulse=abs(ps), sine_a=abs(lr.slope), p_a=lr.pvalue))

Result: blocked, metadata insufficient. Six of the criterion's seven parts are values (means, ranges, ratio, the count of cells with p < 0.0001) measured in the paper's hand-drawn ROIs on the paper's nine cells, and 001274 holds neither the ROIs nor labels for the cells. Both sensitivities are also divided by the paper's nominal fields (257 and 136 V/cm), scaled by the generator voltage, as the files give no measured amplitudes; a wrong field scales every value. Not deciding: sine sensitivity is below pulse sensitivity in all 18 ROIs of the 9 cells under the signed regression (a), and in 15 of 18 under the per-cycle reading (b). With the 12 x 12 boxes the pulse sensitivity averages 17.4 % per kV/cm (range 3.1 to 29.2; paper 28, 15 to 47), the sine sensitivity 5.55 % (0.04 to 14.8; paper 11.8, 1.5 to 28.4) and their ratio 32 % (paper 42 %), and the regression reaches p < 0.0001 in both ROIs in 4 cells, not 8. These values depend on the ROIs, which the paper drew by hand and the files do not hold: with 6 x 6 and 20 x 20 boxes at the same centres the pulse mean is 16.9 and 13.3 %, the sine mean 5.96 and 4.98 %, the ratio 35.2 and 37.6 %, and 1 and 4 cells reach p < 0.0001 in both ROIs; the sine value is below the pulse in 17 and 18 of 18 ROIs. The nine cells are also inferred, not labelled. As for fig4-pooled-time-constants, which was blocked because its values depend on ROIs and a selection the dandiset does not give, the sizes cannot be judged here; they are outside the paper's under every box size and reading, but that is not shown to be a failure of the paper. The carrier phase is assumed zero at the first frame. Fitted freely, the ROI 1 carriers lie at -1.8 to -3.1 rad in all 9 cells and the ROI 2 carriers at 0.1 to 0.9 rad in 7; the two ROIs are near antiphase in those 7, while 4_20240523 is nearly in phase (-2.70 and -2.13 rad) and 2_20240523 in quadrature (-3.14 and 1.56 rad). At the fitted phase the sine sensitivity averages 6.4 to 6.5 % (ratio 37 %), below the pulse value in 18 of 18 ROIs. The pulse files' description puts the pulse onset at frame 20 (1 us), and the mean pulse dF is near 0 before it, rises from frames 20 to 29 and falls after frame 60. The direction holds in every ROI under the signed regression and at the fitted phase, in 15 of 18 under the per-cycle reading, and in 17 or 18 of 18 under every box size; it is the only part that does not rest on the paper's ROIs, and as it fails under the per-cycle reading it cannot carry the claim. Under the per-cycle reading no cell reaches p < 0.0001 in both ROIs. With the full peak-to-peak amplitude, as the criterion names it, the per-cycle sine mean is 13.7 to 16.2 %, the ratio 79 to 93 %, and the sine value is below the pulse in 12 or 13 of 18 ROIs; no row holds.

threshold-depolarization-estimate¶

The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV with FluoVolt's calibration, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.

The mean sine sensitivity of fig6-sine-less-than-pulse times the mean unmodulated 2-kHz threshold of fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher (1-AP or 5-AP, under both field readings), over 1,000, and that times 10 mV per 1%.

Result: blocked, metadata insufficient. The estimate multiplies the 2-kHz AP threshold in V/cm by the sine sensitivity. The threshold in V/cm cannot be formed from the files: they give labelled generator voltages and "1V translates into 36 V/cm" without saying whether of the amplitude or the peak-to-peak value, and they say the delivered amplitude is "somewhat smaller", the calibration not being deposited. The outcome changes with the field reading. Shown, not deciding: with the signed-regression sine sensitivity (5.55 % per kV/cm) and the threshold under the amplitude reading (76.0 V/cm for 1 AP, 90.1 for 5 APs, crop ROI), the emission change is 0.42 to 0.50 %, 4.2 to 5.0 mV; under the peak-to-peak reading it is 0.84 to 1.46 % over the readings; with the paper's own 57.7 V/cm, 0.32 to 0.47 %. In range are 20 of the 24 combinations with the per-cycle slope under the amplitude reading, and none otherwise. The first round recorded this claim as not reproduced.

The Figure 5 and S3 cells (fig5-sine-asymmetry, fig5-whole-cell-depolarization): not identifiable¶

Both claims are about two named cells (C7 and C8 of Figure 6B). The files do not say which cells these are, and the Figure 5 cell's 12 sine sessions match no cell (five at most, in 2_20240522). Shown here, not deciding anything, are the same measures for the nine cells: the correlation of the two ROIs' oscillations and the LOESS fit at the envelope peak (span 2 ms, scaled). The Pearson correlation of the two ROIs' oscillations takes in everything the LOESS leaves, not only the carrier; the carrier alone is compared in fig6-sine-less-than-pulse (fitted phases).

fig3b-low-conductivity-halves-threshold, fig3-extrapolated-threshold¶

Blocked: no dandiset holds 250-ms sessions in the low-conductivity (NaGlu) solution (the solution counts in the data check: 001032, 001033 and 001035 are all NaCl; 001030 holds only the 2-s ramped waves). The extrapolation depends on these thresholds.

AP detector variants¶

The claims file's O3 asks for a "width at half height of 2 to 20 ms". The width can be taken at half the peak's dF (its height above F0) or at half its prominence (its rise above the neighbouring troughs). Each alone fails on these traces in a way the other catches: at half the dF a small wiggle on the tail of an AP counts as another AP 5 ms later, and at half the prominence (the first round's detector) small oscillations on a raised plateau count as APs, so that no session can show a sustained depolarization. The detector used above asks for 2 to 20 ms under both (tisine.detect_aps). This cell reruns the time-lapse claims under each single measure, for ROI c and F0 a.

In [42]:
VAR = []
for wr in ["both", "height", "prominence"]:
    T = {d: ts.session_table(REC[d], d, wr) for d in ["001032", "001033", "001035", "001271"]}
    F = pd.concat([T[d] for d in ["001032", "001033", "001035"]], ignore_index=True)
    F = F[F.kind.isin(["sine", "mod"]) & F.carrier.isin([2000.0, 20000.0])].copy()
    F["stim"] = np.where(F["kind"] == "mod", "mod", "pure") + "_" + (F.carrier / 1000).astype(int).astype(str) + "k"
    for o3 in "ab":
        r = ("c", "a", o3); g = rd(F, r)
        f1 = fig1(g); th = thresholds(g)
        pv = {}
        for car, k in [("2k", "t5"), ("20k", "t1"), ("20k", "t5")]:
            m = th[th.stim == f"mod_{car}"][k].dropna(); p_ = th[th.stim == f"pure_{car}"][k].dropna()
            pv[f"p_mod_{car}_{k}"] = stats.ttest_ind(m, p_).pvalue if len(m) > 1 and len(p_) > 1 else np.nan
        c = g.groupby(["neuron", "carrier", "volts", "kind"]).n_ap.mean().unstack("kind").dropna()
        bb = block(g, "b"); bt = beats(g, "b", F); tt = ttx(r, "b", T["001271"]); tt = tt[tt.common_volts > 0]
        f3 = judge(fig3c("c", "a", o3, "c7_free", wr), "b")
        VAR.append(dict(width=wr, o3=o3, excited_2k=f1["excited_2k"], excited_20k=f1["excited_20k"], latency_med=f1["median_latency_at_threshold"],
                        rho_neg=f"{f1['rho_neg']}/{f1['n_rho']}", max_rate_med=f1["max_rate_median"], block_b=f"{int(bb.sustained.sum())}/{len(bb)}",

                        fig3c_block=sum(v["block"] for v in f3.values()), **pv))

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • The data are the ten dandisets the paper lists, not 001048, which names the paper but holds another study. Every claim is data: elsewhere.
  • The soma ROI: the crop the depositors cut around the soma (16 x 16 pixels) is used as the main reading, with the claims file's Otsu readings shown; the paper's ROIs are not deposited.
  • AP detection, sustained depolarization and the windows follow the claims file's readings; the paper identified APs by eye. The AP width at half height is required to be 2 to 20 ms both at half the peak's dF and at half its prominence (an assumption; each alone is shown as a variant).
  • Where the ROI readings give different outcomes, the crop ROI decides, as an assumption (protocol step 1.6), where the claims file's header would block.
  • Where the O4 readings give different outcomes (fig2-modulated-locks-to-beats only), half the neuron's median AP height (O4 b) decides, as an assumption.
  • Fields are labelled generator voltages, not calibrated amplitudes; the conversion to V/cm uses the files' 36 V/cm per volt under two readings.
  • Strobe ROIs are 12 x 12 pixel boxes at the extremes of the smoothed ratio image (6 x 6 and 20 x 20 as a variant), flash intensity is scaled to the image median (no debris ROI is marked), and the fields are the paper's 257 and 136 V/cm, scaled by the generator voltage for the two cells run at other voltages.
  • The 19 Figure 4 experiments and the Figure 5 and S3 cells cannot be identified in the files.

What was found about the datasets:

  • 001048, the dandiset that names the paper, holds HEK-cell TIRF recordings of another study.
  • 001034 is a copy of 001032: all 178 recordings are identical, under other subject names.
  • 001030 states mouse neurons (C57BL/6), where the paper used rat neurons; 001035 calls its neurons "C57BL/6 rat"; 001030 makes each session a separate subject.
  • The voltages are not calibrated: the files say the true amplitude is smaller by frequency-dependent factors "reported separately", which are not in the dandisets.
  • No low-conductivity (NaGlu) recordings with 250-ms waves are deposited, so Figures 3A and 3B cannot be tested; 001272 holds 3 of the 8 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons.
  • The dandisets hold stimuli the paper does not describe (20-Hz to 10-kHz sine waves in 001032, 001033 and 001035, 40-kHz sine waves in 001033 and 100-kHz ones in 001035; 100-kHz pulses in 001031; TTX strobe sessions in 001274).
  • The TTX session descriptions say TTX "caused sustained depolarization", the opposite of the paper and of the dandiset's own description; the vehicle neurons carry no mark of when the vehicle was applied; the Di-8-ANEPPS sessions of 001272 are all described as "vehicle control".
  • Strobe files hold no ROIs, no cell shape or orientation labels and no stimulus waveforms.
  • 001273 gives the delivered amplitudes of its pulses in a note (25, 62, 79 and 102 V for 40, 80, 100 and 130 V), where the paper gives 140 V/cm for every experiment.
